name: Clay-with-flints (the stiff red-brown clay over the chalk)

diffuseAlbedo.source: Colour name: Wikipedia 'Clay-with-Flints' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay-with-Flints), Loveday's definition 'yellowish red or red-brown clay'; BGS Lexicon, Clay-with-flints Formation (https://webapps.bgs.ac.uk/lexicon/lexicon.cfm?pub=CWF): 'orange-brown and red-brown sandy clay'. Munsell renotation real.dat (http://www.rit-mcsl.org/MunsellRenotation/real.dat): 5YR 4/6 x 0.4651, y 0.3859, Y 12.000
diffuseAlbedo.note: The choice of value 4 within 'yellowish red' is a judgement, not a measurement. 'Red-brown' would be redder (2.5YR). No colour of the site's own clay was measured, and a field Munsell reading of soil is normally of moist soil, so a dry face would be lighter.
diffuseAlbedo.derivation: 5YR 4/6 is the Munsell soil name 'yellowish red'. xyY (C) = (0.4651, 0.3859, 0.1200) converted to XYZ, then Bradford adaptation from C (0.31006, 0.31616) to D65, then CIELAB D65. I recomputed this independently and got [41.2, 18.6, 30.6]. 7.5YR 5/6 (x 0.4440, y 0.3954, Y 19.77) gives [51.6, 14.5, 34.8], also confirmed.

refractiveIndex.source: Handbook of Mineralogy, 'Kaolinite', https://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/pdfs/kaolinite.pdf: alpha = 1.553-1.565, beta = 1.559-1.569, gamma = 1.560-1.570 (opened; confirmed)
refractiveIndex.derivation: Mean of the three range midpoints: (1.559 + 1.564 + 1.565)/3 = 1.5627, rounded to 1.563
refractiveIndex.note: This assumes a kaolinitic clay, and no source on the clay mineralogy of Clay-with-flints was read. If the clay fraction is rich in smectite (montmorillonite about 1.48 to 1.53), the value would be about 0.03 to 0.05 lower. The quartz sand (1.547) changes it by less than 0.02.

porosity.source: A stiff clay's porosity, 0.40 to 0.50 (a first middle value)

wettingDepth.note: The depth whose pores govern the face's look when wet.

grain.source: Docs/Stages/cube.md section 7 (the ground rule's relief and stones)
grain.note: The finest structure the face shows.

bed.source: Docs/Stages/cube.md section 7 (the ground rule's relief and stones)
bed.note: The coarsest structure the face shows.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the topsoil's.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
